input.question: Why families don't move thousands of miles away from that Yellowstone volcano with so much drilling, fracking and earthquakes so close to it ?
input.ground_truth: Think about it this way; what if I asked you to uproot your entire life, leave your work, leave your house, friends, family. Can you afford to do this? Can you get a new job elsewhere? It's a lot easier to stay for most people.

Question: Why families don't move thousands of miles away from that Yellowstone volcano with so much drilling, fracking and earthquakes so close to it ?

response.prediction:
Okay! Let’s imagine the Yellowstone volcano is like a big, sleepy giant under the ground. Sometimes, when people do things like drilling and fracking (which is like poking and shaking the ground to get oil or gas), it can make the giant wake up a little and shake (those are the earthquakes).

Now, even though the giant (volcano) is very far away from most people’s homes, it’s still a very, very big and powerful giant. If it gets really upset, it could cause a lot of trouble, like making the ground shake a LOT and sending out hot stuff.

So, families don’t want to move right next to the giant because if it wakes up and gets angry, it could hurt a lot of people, even if it’s far away. It’s like not wanting to play too close to a big, sleepy dog that might wake up and bark really loud and scare everyone.

Also, even though there’s drilling and fracking happening, scientists and grown-ups try to make sure it’s done safely and not too close to the volcano, because they want to keep everyone safe.

So, families stay away from the volcano to be safe, just in case the giant decides to wake up and cause a big problem!
